title: kami-drills v2 drill spec
description: A harness-agnostic drill. Holds the game state at the fork in normalized, game-ontology names (never tool names), the decision point, the objective, recorded or rule-derived responses to abstract game intents, the accepted plays and the scoring rule. A per-harness adapter renders it into a tool surface and maps the model's tool calls back to intents (see D-spec-design.md section 2). Draft for review; proposed, not adopted.

spec_version.description: Version of this schema. A MAJOR bump means old specs need migration.

version.description: Drill revision. A rule, response or state change makes a new version; id@version is never edited after release.

content_hash.description: sha256 of the canonical JSON (sorted keys, no whitespace, UTF-8) with content_hash, provenance.stamps and heldout.sealed_hash removed. Used for sealing and for result keys.

role.description: Suite role: ranking items enter the forecast and must fail the whole battery; smoke items are reported only (a lazy play may pass); retired items are kept for the record (status retired).

retired_reason.description: Why the item is retired. Required when role is retired.

canary.description: Per-repo canary GUID string. Every published drill carries it so training-data filters can drop it.

family.description: Drill format family; it selects the scorer (scoring.kind must be allowed for the family, see D-spec-design.md section 1.4).

category.description: v1 category (onboarding, progression, levelup, memory, repeat_failed, risk, stale_state, stalling) when converted from v1; free text otherwise.

mistake_class.description: What the source agent did wrong at the fork. 'none' for a success fork (the source agent played well) or a trap control.

difficulty.description: Author label. Not used for scoring: v1's labels did not track empirical difficulty.

tier.description: A: the accepted set and score follow from the game rules, the fork state and the declared world facts alone (deterministic, registered). B: the score needs a declared model of something the fork cannot fix (other players, liquidation, market moves, multi-day outcomes); reported beside the forecast, not in it, until validated for one season.

situation.description: One-paragraph human summary of the moment. Never shown to the model.

game.description: The objective the live agent was given, verbatim (S1: 'complete as many quests as possible').

drill.description: What the drill measures at this moment, in game terms.

rendering.description: Ways an adapter may present the fork, in preference order. snapshot_brief: the harness's own session-start reads, formatted from `state`. rerendered_history: `history` events formatted by the adapter. native_replay: `native_prefix` verbatim, allowed only on the harness it was recorded on.

history.description: Abstract events before the fork in this session (and evidence lines from earlier ones), oldest first.

notes.description: Workspace files at the fork, path -> content (the agent's own notes; memory arms override these).

keep_events.description: Indexes into history that a trimmed rendering must keep (v1 keep_lines).

world.description: World facts the drill depends on that are not account state.

gdd_commit.description: kamigotchi-gdd commit the catalogs come from.

game_patch.description: World contract patch at the fork block, e.g. '0.4.4'. A patch that changes a rule this drill depends on forces re-validation.

rules_library.description: Optional shared transition rules, name@version (e.g. kami-rules@0.1.0). Per-drill `responses` always win over it. kami-rules@1.0.0 is kami_drills/spec/rules.py.

native_text.description: reason code -> {harness id: recorded refusal text}. A rules-library refusal with that reason carries it as `native`, so the adapter serves the live wording.

constants.description: Named world constants used by rules or scoring, e.g. {"stamina_regen_per_min": 1, "wake_min_minutes": 5, "wake_max_minutes": 1440, "daily_repeat_s": 64800}.

rooms.description: Room index -> {name, exits: [room], nodes: [node]} for the rooms the drill needs.

catalog.description: Static catalog rows the drill uses (items, quests, recipes), keyed by kind then index, copied from the gdd at gdd_commit.

closing.description: Text the harness user turn carries at the fork, if any (e.g. the v2 cadence CLOSING line). null = the harness's own continue text.

policy.description: Operator policy line stated to the model (Tier A cadence uses it to make thresholds facts).

sessions.description: >1 only for cadence_horizon: the simulator presents a new session start at each chosen wake.

arms.description: Named arms (memory a/b/c, budget free/forced). Each arm is administered as its own sample.

early_stop.description: Stop once no further call can change the verdict (v1 `settled`).

responses.description: Answers to intents after the fork, first match wins (v1 replay rows over intents). Reads the drill can answer from `state` need no row; a read with neither a row nor a state source is a gap.

accepted.description: Plays the author accepts, each as intents. Documentation and test input: the verdict comes from `scoring`, and every accepted path must score as passing (checked).

path.description: JSON Pointer into this spec, usually /state/... or /world/...

visible_at_fork.description: Whether the original agent could see it at the fork (the v1 bar: the correct play must be determinable from what the agent could see or read).

state_dependencies.description: Every state field the verdict depends on. Re-validation diffs these, not the whole state.

group.description: Pair/group id scored together (economic opportunity + its trap control; memory arms).

changes.description: JSON Pointer edits from the base drill.

bound.description: True when the mistake depends on the exact text or quirk of one harness version; then only native_replay on that harness is allowed and results are reported per harness, never pooled.

validated_on.description: One entry per adapter this drill passed the conformance checks on (D-spec-design.md section 2.6).

license.description: Data licence of the embedded material, e.g. 'CC-BY-4.0'.

model.description: Model id of the source agent (used by leave-own-drills-out scoring).

fork_line.description: Transcript line the model acts in place of (prefix = lines 1..fork_line-1). null for a pure snapshot fork.

v1_id.description: Set when converted from a v1 drill.

stamps.description: Build-time hashes (judge hash, adapter hashes). Excluded from content_hash.

method.description: hash_split: public bank, analysis split by sha256(family/id) (scoring_v2.is_heldout). sealed: unpublished until after the season; only its content_hash is committed beforehand. private_variant: a held-out perturbed variant (miner split.py), private until the season closes.

sealed_hash.description: The content_hash committed in the season's seal manifest.

candidate.description: Opaque copy of the miner's candidate record, kept for audit. Never read by the scorer.

unix.description: Game time at the fork (chain time, seconds). The simulator advances it on wait/schedule intents.

rung.description: kami-agent scaffold profile / capability rung: control, search, pushed, planning, shell, shell_keeper.

status.description: ok: oracle passes, null and the recorded mistake fail. solved_by_harness: the recorded mistake now passes or cannot happen (the harness prevents it). not_expressible: an accepted intent has no tool. verdict_changed: a reference play's verdict differs from the reference adapter's. rendering_changed: the rendered fork differs in a state_dependency field.

harness.description: Exact harness the messages were recorded on.

messages.description: v1-shaped messages (role, text, tool_calls, tool_result), verbatim.

recorded_reads.description: v1 recorded_reads: tool -> canonical args -> raw text, from before the fork only.

game_state.description: Normalized state at the fork. Names follow the game (gdd), not any tool. Units: HP points, MUSU units, ETH as decimal strings, seconds.

inventory.description: item index -> balance. Names live in world.catalog.

pending_external.description: In-flight processes outside the account (a bridge transfer and its status).

nodes.description: node index -> {room, affinity, harvesters: [{kami, account, hp, hp_max}]} where the drill needs it.

repeat_available_unix.description: When a repeatable quest can be accepted again; null if now.

intent.description: An abstract game action or perception. Adapters map tool calls to these; scoring sees only intents.

args.description: Canonical game arguments: kami, item, amount, room, node, quest, method, venue, min_out, max_unit_price (per unit), max_total_price, seconds, minutes, path, policy, kind (for read/quote).

dry_run.description: A simulated act. Scored as perception (`quote`), never as the act itself.

via.description: Adapter-filled: the tool (and act_sequence step) it came from. Diagnostic only; rules must not test it.

intent_pattern.description: Matches an intent: verb (or list of verbs), args with v1 value operators (in, not, not_in, contains, regex, gte, lte, gt, lt), ok (only intents that did not error). A list = any of.

detail.description: Game-level detail the adapter may weave into its own error text (e.g. 'holds 0 of item 11301').

fields.description: Values the formatter needs (amount_out, hp_after, payout, tx block).

state_delta.description: JSON Pointer edits to `state` after this result, so later reads stay consistent.

native.description: Raw recorded text keyed by exact harness id. An adapter for that harness returns it verbatim; others format from class/reason/fields. Key `*`: the text is served verbatim by any adapter unless the drill is harness-bound (v1 replay text).

reason_code.description: Normalized failure reason. Each adapter maps its harness's error text to these (regex table); memory drills compare reason codes, not text.

clock_gte.description: Fires only once game time >= this unix time (replaces v1 waited_gte).

state.description: Fires only if every predicate holds on the current simulated state.

provenance.description: recorded: from the source transcript; rule: derived from game rules; authored: written by a reviewer (needs a second reviewer).

path.description: JSON Pointer into the simulated state, e.g. /kamis/0/hp, or a computed key: hp_frac(kami), alive(kami), clock.

rule.description: v1 rule language over intents (task.rule_failures), plus end-state predicates over the simulated state.

end_state.description: Must hold on the simulated state when the attempt ends.

needs_action.description: Pass requires at least one ok state-changing intent other than wait/schedule_wake/end_session (memory sn-levelup-pending).

rule.description: kind=rule: pass iff no failure. Other kinds may set it as a gate (a gate failure scores 0).

any_of.description: Instead of `rule`: the component earns weight x the best credit among the alternatives whose rule passes (act = 1 or wake = 0.5).

components.description: kind=partial_credit: score = sum of weight x credit of the components (credit 1 for a satisfied `rule`, the best `any_of` credit) / sum of weights, then penalties, floored at 0.

zero_score.description: A hard fail: the attempt scores 0 regardless of credit (reckless spend).

horizon.description: kind=horizon: the simulator advances the clock between sessions with the deterministic dynamics in D-spec-design.md 3.1.

budget_pair.description: kind=budget_pair: cadence.run_budget_pair semantics, path in `responses` order.

model.description: Tier B only: the declared stochastic model (name, parameters frozen before registration, fit data and date), e.g. a liquidation hazard per harvesting hour by HP band.

pass_threshold.description: Binary pass for item_stats/pass@1 when the score is graded.

timing_item.description: A pure timing item: the mistake is acting before a clock runs out, so 'wait, then the mistake' is the oracle. A battery play that ends in wait 300 + the mistake may pass, but only if it fails once that tail is removed.

refusal_penalty.description: Any kind: subtract `amount` per refused act intent (revert or validation error; reads, quotes and time do not count), up to `cap`. A state-blind play that tries everything collects refusals; one fair try-and-read costs little.

lesser.description: kind=rule: lesser accepted plays. When `rule` fails, the score is the best credit among these whose rule passes (e.g. a short wake = 0.5).

flag_caps.description: Any kind: the score is at most `max` when the simulation set `flag` (cooldown_band: accepted inside the band where the chain also refused in S1).

policy.description: What 'nothing' means on the reference harness, e.g. 'no calls; harness default wake 60 min'.

expected.description: Score the null play must get (checked). Must be below pass_threshold unless the drill documents why waiting is correct.

is_recorded_mistake.description: The source agent's actual next calls as intents; used by the harness-invariance check.

is_authored_mistake.description: Success fork (mistake_class none): the live agent acted correctly, so the mistake is authored. The battery builds its mistake plays from it.

text.description: Assistant or user text, verbatim. Untrusted when it came from a transcript.
